title: What they said at the time

clips.q: We never expected to do this well and be this well-received.
The version of OUYA shipping now should be considered a beta release, and anyone hoping for anything more is in for some disappointment.
The demand we’re seeing from gamers and our retailers is beyond our expectations.
Retail sales for Ouya […] were relatively light for a new console.
clips.who: **Liam Callahan**, NPD analyst, as reported by MCV, Jul 19, 2013[^12]

clips.q: Sales have been surprisingly high for a new game on a new console.
clips.who: **Matt Thorson**, developer of TowerFall, quoted by MCV, Jul 22, 2013[^13]

clips.q: The truth is, openness is hard.
clips.who: **Julie Uhrman**, on the Free the Games Fund, quoted by Game Developer, Sep 11, 2013[^15]

clips.q: Being the best game on Ouya isn’t a huge deal, but it is nice. It still sells on there.
clips.who: **Matt Thorson**, to Eurogamer, quoted by MCV, Apr 29, 2014[^21]

clips.q: We believe we’ve built something real and valuable.
clips.who: **Julie Uhrman**, memo to investors, quoted by Fortune, Apr 28, 2015[^24]

clips.q: Razer is the perfect home for OUYA and the team that made it all happen.
clips.who: **Julie Uhrman**, in Razer’s press release, Jul 27, 2015[^25]

clips.q: Razer kept the OUYA store running post-acquisition, a ghost of its former self.
